text:
maria: Noticed a 99.9th tail blip around 22:12 UTC. Heatmap shows prefill waves overlapping on shelf-12 in us-west1, NVMe/io and PCIe counters spike together.
ajay: Confirmed. Seen increased PCIe retransmits + DMA bursts on shelf-12 around the same timeframe. Likely prefill/co-located onboarding bursts.
sam: Any single tenant dominating, or is this multi-tenant churn?
maria: Traces show heavy concurrent warmups from tenants t-77, t-88, and an onboarding job t-512 triggered by growth ramp. Mixed traffic.
linh: Shelf-12 is also hosting 3 latency-sensitive prod slices. We should avoid mixing warmup-heavy tenants with prod on same shelf.
ajay: Short-term mitigation proposal: carve out a temporary "warmup-exempt" tag for prod and set prefill routing to avoid shelves with prod tag. I can flip an allocator rule.
sam: Or throttle prefill concurrency globally in us-west1 to reduce DMA peaks. Which impacts less?
linh: Throttle impacts onboarding duration; carveout risks capacity fragmentation and cost. Prefer throttling as immediate step, then plan a dedicated warmup-shelf approach.
maria: Agree. Throttle first. opsbot: please apply.
opsbot: action: set-config prefill-controller --region=us-west1 --max-concurrent-warmups=4 (requested by @maria)
ajay: Running canary probe on shelf-12 metrics endpoint: `curl -s http://metrics.local/node/shelf-12/pcie | jq .tail` to watch realtime.
(60s)
ajay: pcie tail down ~42%, DMA bursts reduced. Prod latency stabilized.
sam: OK short-term success. Need follow-ups:
- allocator change to prefer "warmup shelves" (rule example below)
- labeling onboarding jobs with "prefill-heavy" so allocator can avoid prod shelves
- cost estimate for reserving 1-2 shelves in us-west1 for warmup

Proposed allocator rule (prototype):
```
PATCH /allocator/rules
{
  "match": { "job_type": "warmup", "tenant_label": "prefill-heavy" },
  "action": { "preferred_shelves": ["warmup-shelf-a", "warmup-shelf-b"] }
}
```

linh: I'll draft RFC `warmup-shelf-proposal` with traffic model and delta cost. We should include fallback: if warmup shelves full then degrade warmup concurrency rather than spill into prod.
maria: Assigning INC-2026-215 to track root cause & follow-ups (throttle applied, RFC planned).
ajay: Also observed a loose correlation with nightly backup jobs (~22:00) causing NVMe IO that amplifies PCIe contention. We should mark backup windows in allocator to lower warmup concurrency.
maria: Good catch. Will sync with infra-sched to annotate maintenance/backups. @mica (growth), fyi this will throttle some onboarding speed — expect a slight UX delay.
mica: Thanks for the heads-up. We'll surface to product and consider increasing credits for high-volume onboards to offset slower warmups.
sam: Long-term: either (A) dedicated warmup shelves, (B) allocator improvements to avoid hot co-locations, or (C) hybrid: ephemeral warmup slices + graceful backoff. Prioritize A+B in RFC.
linh: I'll include benchmarks: warmup time vs. cost for 0,1,2 reserved shelves.
opsbot: deploybot: applied config change across us-west1 prefill-controller (3 controllers) successfully.
maria: Monitoring for 30m. If stable, we'll leave throttle and move to RFC. Thanks team :thumbsup:
